attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his own newsletter post, stated as his analysis rather than quoted from someone else.

semantics.note: Keeps the 190GW planning figure, the $1.62–2.92T range, the best-case $110B demand, the 90%+ concentration and the claim of exclusive VC dependence. It is a compound present-state estimate, so observation is the right kind.

contract.note: The plain reading is fair and ordinary: the two companies are OpenAI and Anthropic, demand means compute spending, Q2 2026 is the reference period, and the figures are estimates. The result turns on unstated conversion assumptions and on how demand is defined, which the contract flags. Requiring proof of exclusive VC dependence matches his strong wording.

evidence.note: Sightline (Feb 2026) tracks 190GW announced since 2024. This is the likely source of his figure but counts all announced capacity, not just planned. It says nothing on spending required or on demand.

Bessemer splits the 190GW into ~148GW planned, ~21GW under construction and ~12GW operational. That suggests 'in planning' is loose wording, but it does not test the spending range, the demand ceiling or the concentration figure.

Epoch's tentative estimate that the two labs had 15–20% of physical AI compute at end-2025 measures a different metric (physical share, not spending share) and an earlier period, so it cannot directly contradict the 90%+ spending share.

reviews.rationale: No item gives a model turning 190GW into annual spending needs, an industry-wide compute-demand total, a matching base for the 90% share, or financing records on VC dependence. The capacity sources and Epoch's figures concern different scopes or metrics, so they are context only. The packet does not settle the claim.
